title: The Sum of All Summaries: PROPALIGN for Graded Proposition Salience Evaluation
abstract: arXiv:2610.19387v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Identification and ranking of salient propositions in documents is indirectly involved in many AI tasks, but few papers define proposition salience scores clearly, make diverse data available, or evaluate models directly on the task. This paper proposes PROPALIGN, a multiple-summary-based approach for propositional salience score estimation, and releases PROPALIGNBANK, an accompanying dataset for the method with 138K alignments of over 35K propositions. We compare several approaches to salient proposition extraction in English across a broad range of spoken and written genres, and demonstrate that naively asking models for judgments leads to inconsistencies. By contrast, graded, summary-based metrics are more stable. We further observe that while single models perform worse than humans, an ensemble of models incorporating linguistic features approaches manual annotation quality ceilings. translated_abstract: 文档中显著命题的识别与排序间接参与了许多人工智能任务，但很少有论文清晰地定义命题显著性分数、提供多样化的数据，或直接在该任务上评估模型。本文提出了PROPALIGN，一种基于多个摘要的命题显著性分数估计方法，并发布了与之配套的数据集PROPALIGNBANK，其中包含超过3.5万个命题的13.8万条对齐数据。我们在英语中跨越广泛的口语和书面文体比较了几种显著命题提取方法，并证明简单地要求模型作出判断会导致结果不一致。相比之下，分级的、基于摘要的指标更加稳定。我们进一步观察到，虽然单个模型的表现不如人类，但结合语言特征的模型集成方法接近人工标注的质量上限。此外，对模型输出的分析表明
tldr: 本文提出基于多摘要的分级命题显著性评分方法PROPALIGN及配套数据集PROPALIGNBANK，证明摘要式评分比直接询问模型更稳定，且结合语言特征的模型集成可接近人工标注质量上限。
en_tdlr: PROPALIGN introduces a graded, multiple-summary-based approach to proposition salience scoring with its dataset PROPALIGNBANK, showing that summary-based metrics are more stable than direct model judgments and that model ensembles with linguistic features approach human annotation quality ceilings.
